title: NFTMigrator.migrate(): per-quantity mintFor loop scales O(balance) and can become un-callable for large V1 holders
description: migrate() iterates over every V1 dispatcher index (outer loop bounded by v1.nextIndex()) and, for any held balance, calls v2.mintFor(v2Index, msg.sender) once per unit of balance (inner loop `for (uint256 j = 0; j < balance; j++)`). Each mintFor performs an external CALL into NFTMinterV2, runs onlyAuthorizedMinter check, executes ERC1155 _mint (storage write + ERC1155Receiver callback if recipient is a contract), and emits ClaimMintedFor. ERC1155 _mint costs roughly 25k-50k gas warm, so a holder of 1000 V1 NFTs of a single index pays ~30M-50M gas to migrate — close to or above the Ethereum block gas limit. A power user (e.g. a market maker who bulk-bought V1 NFTs) may find migrate() un-callable. The single-tx design also means a holder cannot partially migrate; they either migrate everything successfully or nothing.
exploit_path:
1. Alice (or a treasury that aggregated V1 NFTs) holds 800 V1 NFTs across two indexes (e.g. 500 of v1Index=1 and 300 of v1Index=2).
2. Alice calls migrate(). The contract burns 500 v1 NFTs of index 1, then enters the inner loop and calls v2.mintFor 500 times. With each mintFor at ~30k gas, the inner loop alone consumes ~15M gas before even reaching index 2.
3. The tx hits the block gas limit (~30M on mainnet) and reverts. Alice's V1 NFTs were never burned (the burn precedes the mints in the same tx, so the revert rolls back both) but she also cannot migrate via any other path because migrate() is the only entry point.
4. Alice is effectively locked out of migration. Workaround would be to transfer V1 NFTs to fresh addresses and migrate piecewise, but that requires Alice to set up multiple wallets and pay multiple gas premiums.

This is a UX / availability issue rather than a theft, but it can permanently strand large V1 holders if the V1 supply distribution is concentrated.
mainnet_realism_check: Mainnet gas limit is ~30M. ERC1155 _mint cost is well-known. No mock dependency.
recommendation: Replace the inner per-unit loop with a single _mintBatch / _mint call that takes `balance` as quantity. NFTMinterV2.mintFor currently always mints 1; introduce a mintForBatch(index, recipient, quantity) variant authorized minters can use, then NFTMigrator becomes O(numIndexes) instead of O(numIndexes * totalBalance). Alternatively, allow migrate() to take a list of specific indexes so users can split the migration across multiple txs.
severity_rationale: Confirmed Low/QA. UX/availability issue: large V1 NFT holders (>~1000 of a single index) may hit block-gas-limit when calling migrate() because the per-unit inner loop performs full mintFor() calls. No assets at risk — V1 NFTs are not burned if the tx reverts. The workaround is wallet-splitting before migration. This is an efficiency/availability concern for power users. Per C4 QA: ineffeciency / availability-edge concern fits Low.
